choices.detail: Outrun the thief, the fog and the ray.
choices.outcome: The Marigold leaps forward.

illustration.alt: A young coupler with a hand lamp stands before a frost-covered door with no handle. A small glowing hand-shaped panel sits in a swirl of frost.

nodes.title: Every lantern lit
paragraphs: The last verse climbs, and everybody climbs with it. The crew sings. The Moths sing from seven decks. Ember sings loudest of all, and Old Gold answers with a light so bright that the Shiver turns gold from edge to edge. The track into Halfway Bell shines out as clear as noon.

Halvard brakes on that light and stops the Marigold dead on the platform mark. Vane, dazzled, lets go of Car 13 and drifts straight into Sable's nets, skiff and all, with the three frozen eggs unharmed. And out of the fog, drawn by the song, come three more great rays, each to collect her own.
Within the week, Lanterns 38 to 41 are burning again. The Company signs a treaty with the Lamplighters. PIP adds a new line to the manifest: CAR 13, NURSERY.
And on the hook above your bunk, next to your badge, hangs a patched coat with a hundred tiny mirrors. It's exactly your size.

ending.title: Every lantern lit
ending.note: BEST OUTCOME · All four eggs go home, the thief is caught and every lantern shines.

illustration.alt: An enormous ray with rivers of gold light along its wings fills the sky above the tiny star train and the grey ships.

nodes.title: The coupler who jumped
paragraphs: Six kicks, in the right order. Four claws spring open together and Car 13 swings free, still coupled, still singing. The skiff, with nothing left to hold, drops like a stone into seven waiting nets. Vane is inside it. So are you and Wick, which wasn't exactly the plan.

From Sable's deck you watch the rest. The roof of Car 13 slides open. Ember rises, small and gold, and Old Gold folds one enormous wing around it. In the Fleet's nets, three frosted cases glow softly, safe.

But the Marigold, braking late with no coupler aboard, slides clean through Halfway Bell and has to be towed back half a day later. Twenty-two years of perfect arrivals, gone. The Conductor says it was worth it. She says it through her teeth.
The Moths will carry the three eggs home, one lantern at a time. Sable offers you a berth for the season. Brandt signs your leave slip herself: ON LOAN. RETURN IN ONE PIECE.

ending.title: The coupler who jumped
ending.note: GREAT OUTCOME · All four eggs are safe and the thief is caught, but the Marigold misses its station.

illustration.alt: Two children in vacuum suits, one in a coat of tiny mirrors, stand on the golden roof of the moving train in the fog.

nodes.title: The wrong three
paragraphs: You hold on. The skiff's engine fires, the claws tear, and Car 13 comes off the Marigold like a loose tooth. For a moment thief, coupler, Lamplighter and nursery all tumble through the fog together. Then the nets close.

The Moths catch the skiff. They catch you and Wick, three sleeping eggs and one very quiet thief. They don't catch Car 13. It spins away into the Shiver, frost glittering, with a small gold light at its roof vent. Old Gold turns and goes after it.
Three eggs go home. Three lanterns will burn again. Nobody knows what became of the fourth, or of the mother who followed it into the dark.
Wick says rays always find their own. She says it every night, like a verse of the song.

ending.title: The wrong three
ending.note: MIXED OUTCOME · Three eggs are saved and the thief is caught, but Ember and Old Gold vanish into the Shiver.

illustration.alt: An enormous ray with rivers of gold light along its wings fills the sky above the tiny star train and the grey ships.

nodes.title: The long way round
paragraphs: You open the roof of Car 13. Frost whirls out into the dark, and Ember rises with it, small and gold and suddenly sure. Old Gold curls one enormous wing around the little light, as gently as a hand around a match. Her glow brightens just enough to show you the track.

The Marigold comes into Halfway Bell slow and safe: twelve cars and one empty nursery. But in the confusion Vane cuts his claws loose, and the black skiff slips away into the Shiver with three frozen eggs still aboard.
Lantern 41 is shining again by the time you head for home. Lanterns 38, 39 and 40 are not.

Wick stands at the lamp car rail, watching the dark. “Three to go,” she says. The Conductor hands her a crew badge. “Then we'd better keep counting,” says Brandt, and she looks at you when she says it.

ending.title: The long way round
ending.note: GOOD OUTCOME · Ember is home and everyone is safe, but the thief escapes with three eggs.

illustration.alt: A small glowing golden ray floats above a glass cradle in a car full of icicles and frost ferns.

nodes.title: A hard stop
paragraphs: “Everything, Halvard. Now!” The brakes scream. Sparks pour from under every car. The Marigold stops at Halfway Bell with a jolt that throws every pot in the galley, and Car 13, caught between the brakes and the skiff's claws, splits open like a walnut.

Wick catches Ember in her coat as the frost garden scatters into space. Vane's skiff spins off into the fog, dented, with its cases still aboard. And Old Gold, startled by the noise and the sparks, veers away into the Shiver before anyone can call her back.
Ember is safe. The crew is safe. But the Marigold will spend a whole season in the repair dock.
A small gold ray rides with the Moth Fleet now. Every night it sings three notes going up, then one long one, out into the dark, for a mother who is still out there searching.

ending.title: A hard stop
ending.note: ROUGH OUTCOME · Ember and the crew are safe, but Car 13 is wrecked and Old Gold is lost in the fog.

nodes.title: Twelve cars
paragraphs: You pull the lever. It's the easiest coupling you have ever undone. Car 13 slides away from the train, small and frosted, and Vane's skiff hauls it off into the fog like a fisherman with his catch. A gold light shows at the roof vent for a moment. Then it's gone.
The Marigold, lighter by one car, brakes easily and glides into Halfway Bell right on time. Twelve cars. The list is correct. Nobody on the platform will ever know there was a thirteenth.
But Old Gold turns away to follow the skiff into the dark, and behind you four lanterns stay black. By spring, the Company has closed the Line as unsafe.
Wick leaves her tin whistle on your bunk with a note: YOU COUNTED IT. NEXT TIME, KEEP IT. You practise the three notes every night, in case there is a next time.

ending.title: Twelve cars
ending.note: POOR OUTCOME · The train arrives safely, but the eggs are gone and the Lantern Line goes dark.

illustration.alt: A golden star train runs along a line of lanterns in the dark. One car near the tail is white with frost, and one lantern is unlit.

nodes.title: Off the end of the line
paragraphs: “Full throttle!” The Marigold leaps forward. For three glorious seconds you're outrunning everything: the thief, the fog, the great gold ray. Then the worn brakes fail, the track at Halfway Bell flashes past the wrong window, and the train sails off the end of the Line into empty dark.

PIP gets everyone into the lifecar in time. PIP is very good at lists. From its little window you watch the Marigold tumble away car by car, and the black skiff tear loose and vanish with the frozen eggs.
Wick pulled Ember out of Car 13 with seconds to spare. She sits with the little ray zipped inside her coat and doesn't say a word to you.

Old Gold circles the wreck twice, dimming. Then she turns back toward the dark. The Moths tow your lifecar to the starport in silence. There's no train to go home on, and behind you the lanterns are going out, one by one.

ending.title: Off the end of the line
ending.note: WORST OUTCOME · A reckless dash wrecks the Marigold, loses the eggs and darkens the Line.

illustration.alt: A golden star train runs along a line of lanterns in the dark. One car near the tail is white with frost, and one lantern is unlit.

nodes.title: Thirteen, thirteen, thirteen
paragraphs: You count again. Then again from the other end. Then by twos. By the time you've finished counting in a silly voice, the Marigold has left without you, and the platform cleaner is asking you to lift your feet.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE COUNTING)
ending.note: Thirteen is thirteen. Get on the train.

nodes.title: The biscuit of doom
paragraphs: The biscuit is so hard that it chips the tray. You chew for eleven minutes while Tobin watches proudly. Somewhere a mystery goes unsolved while your jaw does all the work.

nodes.title: Among the turnips
paragraphs: You knock, sprint down three cars and dive behind a crate of turnips. Nothing chases you. You wait an hour, to be safe. Turnips are not good company.

ending.title: THE END (OF HIDING)
ending.note: Go back. Try the door properly.

nodes.title: The all-night concert
paragraphs: You shout. Ember copies the shout. Then it copies Tobin's scream, the rattle of the icicles, and the shout again, louder. The concert lasts until breakfast. Nobody can hear anybody explain anything.

nodes.title: The best hiding place on the train
paragraphs: The door seals with a satisfied click. It has no handle on the inside either. You and Tobin spend the night as the coldest, best-hidden people on the Lantern Line. By morning you've built a small, sad snowman.

ending.title: THE END (OF FEELING YOUR TOES)
ending.note: A door with no handle is a poor hiding place.

nodes.title: The white tablecloth
paragraphs: You wave a white tablecloth out of the galley hatch. The grey ships do nothing. The Conductor does plenty. You're assigned to wash that tablecloth, and then every other tablecloth on the train, forever.

nodes.title: A truly wonderful speech
paragraphs: You climb on a galley table and accuse the Inspector in ringing tones. It's a wonderful speech. Vane applauds, thanks you for the warning, and has you shut in the pantry for “disturbing an inspection.” The pantry is full of turnips.

ending.title: THE END (OF YOUR SPEECH)
ending.note: Next time, keep the element of surprise.

nodes.title: Under the bunk
paragraphs: Under your bunk you find two odd socks, a marble, and Tobin, who had the same idea first. You share the marble. The crisis carries on rudely without you.

ending.title: THE END (OF BRAVERY, BRIEFLY)
ending.note: It's crowded under there. Come out.

nodes.title: The soup defence
paragraphs: “That was the soup talking,” you announce. Everyone looks at the soup. The cook is deeply offended. You're sentenced to peel every turnip on the train, and the turnips, as usual, win.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE SOUP DEFENCE)
ending.note: The soup is innocent. Think again.

nodes.title: Forty winks
paragraphs: “We'll think better after a rest,” you say wisely. Everyone lies down. The train does not. You wake up three starports past Halfway Bell with a pillow crease on your face and no memory of the plan.

nodes.title: Noticed
paragraphs: You wave. Something the size of a harbour notices you, personally. It's a bit much. You go and lie down on the galley floor and talk it over with the ceiling for a while.

ending.title: THE END (OF YOUR COMPOSURE)
ending.note: Deep breath. She's friendlier than she looks.

nodes.title: The turnip trade
paragraphs: “Final offer: forty kilos of turnips,” you say into the radio. There's a long silence. “…What kind?” asks Vane. Negotiations drag on all night. Nobody is happy with the result, least of all the turnips.

ending.title: THE END (OF THE TURNIP TRADE)
ending.note: He wants the eggs. Think again.
